text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has dropped nearly 18% over two weeks, with today's small decline continuing a sharp selloff that accelerated after the midterm elections. The broader driver is political: a Democratic sweep in the 2026 midterms has significantly shifted expectations around energy policy, with analysts explicitly flagging that renewable energy (wind and solar) will likely get stronger support while fossil fuel interests face headwinds. For a refiner like Marathon, this raises concerns about long-term demand and regulatory pressure on traditional oil and gas operations.

The immediate refining environment isn't helping—US oil prices have dipped to $99.64 per barrel while refineries are running at 94.5% capacity, which means tighter margins on the fuel they produce. Even though global oil sits higher at $107, that gap reflects a weaker domestic demand picture. The combination of political uncertainty about the energy transition and current margin pressure from the refining side is why the stock has taken such a hard hit in recent days.
